report.tagline: A UK savings and investing app that uses an algorithm to move small amounts from your bank account into savings automatically.
report.simpleSummary: Chip is an app that saves money for you. You connect your bank account, and Chip looks at your income and spending, then quietly moves small amounts it thinks you can afford into savings. Those savings earn interest in accounts held with partner banks. You can also invest in funds, open ISAs, or try a prize savings account where you can win cash.

overview.whatItDoes: Chip helps people save without thinking. Its auto-save feature studies your bank data and moves affordable amounts into a Chip savings pot. It offers easy-access savings, Cash ISAs, a prize savings account, and investment funds and ISAs. It earns from a share of interest, a paid plan, and fees on investments.
howItWorks: You download the app and connect your current account through open banking, which lets Chip read your transactions safely.
Chip's algorithm looks at your balance, income and bills, then picks an amount to save every few days.
You can set how aggressive auto-save is, add one-off deposits, or set regular saves on payday.
Savings sit in accounts with partner banks and are protected up to £85,000 by FSCS.
You can move money into investment funds or a stocks and shares ISA from the same app.
A paid plan, ChipX, unlocks more auto-save options and extra features.
overview.valueProposition: Saving happens automatically at a pace you can afford, so you build a pot without having to remember or decide each time.

businessModel.summary: Chip makes money by keeping part of the interest partner banks pay on savings, by charging a monthly fee for ChipX, and by charging a small yearly fee on investments.

revenueStreams.detail: Partner banks pay interest on deposits; Chip keeps a slice and passes the rest to savers.
A few pounds a month for extra auto-save features.
A yearly percentage of money invested.

businessModel.pricing: Free to save. ChipX is a paid monthly plan of a few pounds a month. Investment accounts have a yearly platform fee plus fund fees. Exact current prices are in the app and change over time.
costDrivers: Marketing to win savers in a crowded market
Open banking and payment costs for each auto-save
Support for withdrawals and account issues
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take a saver with £5,000 at Chip. If partner banks pay around 4.5% and Chip passes 4% to the saver, Chip keeps about 0.5%, or £25 a year. A ChipX subscriber adds maybe £40 to £60 a year. Investment fees on £2,000 might add £5 to £10. If it costs £50 to £100 to win a saver, Chip needs them to stay two years or more. This is why total deposits, now £3 billion, matter so much: revenue grows with the money held.

howTheyGetUsers: Social media ads about painless saving
Crowdfunding rounds that turned users into shareholders and promoters
whatBringsUsersBack: Notifications every time auto-save moves money
growth.moat: Modest. Auto-save is easy to copy, and many banks now have round-ups. Chip's edge is its years of tuning the algorithm, a loyal crowd of user-shareholders, and an all-in-one savings and investing app.

improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of users hitting their goal

pmLessons: Automation removes the hardest part of saving: deciding. Default behaviour is a powerful product lever.
A simple feature can be copied quickly; you need trust, rates or community to stay ahead.
When revenue depends on interest rates, plan for when rates fall.
Letting users control automated features keeps trust high.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you make auto-save save more without upsetting users?
interviewQuestions.hint: Balance savings amount with safety. Use bill data, payday timing and user controls. Guardrail: overdraft rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Compare Chip with Moneybox. Which would you invest in?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare scale, products, revenue mix, profitability and moat. Pick one and explain.

interviewQuestions.question: Interest rates fall to 2%. What happens to Chip and what do you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Revenue and appeal fall. Push investments, ChipX and prize savings. Track deposits and revenue per user.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you get users to move from savings to investing?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find the readiness moment (emergency fund done). Offer education and small first steps. Metric: savings to investment conversion.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Chip's north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Money auto-saved per month. Explain why downloads or deposits alone can mislead.
